title: High-Speed Rail and China's Electric Vehicle Adoption Miracle
abstract: Using China's expansion of the high-speed rail system (HSR) as a quasi-natural experiment, we analyze the comprehensive vehicle registration data from 2010 to 2023 to estimate the causal impact of HSR connectivity on the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs). Implementing several identification strategies, including staggered difference-in-differences (DID), Callaway and Sant'Anna (CS) DID, and two instrumental-variable approaches, we consistently find that, by alleviating range anxiety, the expansion of HSR can account for up to one third of the increase in EV market share and EV sales in China during our sample period, with effects particularly pronounced in cities served by faster HSR lines. The results remain robust when controlling for local industrial policies, charging infrastructure growth, supply-side factors, and economic development. We also find that HSR connectivity amplifies the effectiveness of charging infrastructure and consumer purchase subsidies in promoting EV adoption. Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.
abstract_zh: 本文以中国高速铁路（HSR）系统的扩张作为准自然实验，利用2010至2023年全面的车辆登记数据，估计高铁互联对电动汽车（EV）普及的因果影响。我们采用了多种识别策略，包括交错双重差分（DID）、Callaway和Sant'Anna（CS）双重差分，以及两种工具变量方法，结果一致表明：通过缓解里程焦虑，高铁扩张可以解释样本期内中国电动汽车市场份额和销量增长的多达三分之一，且在高铁线路更快的城市中，这一效应尤为明显。在控制地方产业政策、充电基础设施增长、供给侧因素和经济发展之后，结果依然稳健。我们还发现，高铁互联增强了充电基础设施和消费者购车补贴在推动电动汽车普及方面的效果。美国国家经济研究局（NBER）工作论文系列的机构订阅者，以及发展中国家的居民，可在www.nber.org上免费下载本文，无需额外付费。

title: Online Consumption and Sustained Air Pollution Exposure: Evidence from a Quasi-experiment in China
abstract: This study examines how air pollution affects household consumption in the digital economy. Using a proprietary dataset constructed from more than 500 million online transactions across 291 Chinese cities from 2017 to 2019, we study how online spending changes when pollution rises. To identify causal effects, we exploit quasi-exogenous variation in air quality generated by China’s winter heating policy and implement a difference-in-differences design comparing northern and southern cities around the heating period. We find that pollution increases online spending on health-related products and necessities and reduces spending on non-essential goods. The response is concentrated in the heating period itself, with little evidence of stockpiling before or delayed adjustment afterward. Item-level evidence shows that the increase in spending operates mainly through higher quantities purchased rather than higher payment per item. Additional evidence from Baidu search activity suggests that the spending response is associated with greater attention to pollution risks and protective products, as well as worse mood.
abstract_zh: 本研究考察空气污染如何影响数字经济中的家庭消费。利用一个基于291个中国城市2017至2019年间超过5亿笔网络交易构建的专有数据集，我们研究了污染上升时网络支出如何变化。为识别因果效应，我们利用中国冬季供暖政策带来的准外生空气质量变化，并采用双重差分设计，比较供暖期前后北方与南方城市的情况。我们发现，污染会增加健康相关产品和生活必需品的网络支出，同时减少非必需品支出。这一反应集中出现在供暖期本身，几乎没有囤积或事后延迟调整的证据。商品层面的证据显示，支出增加主要通过购买数量的增加实现，而非单件支付金额的提高。百度搜索数据的补充证据表明，支出反应与人们对污染风险及防护产品的更多关注，以及情绪变差相关。

Nudges from School Children and Electricity Conservation: Evidence from the 'Project Carbon Zero' Campaign in Singapore
abstract: Can children effectively nudge their parents to change their energy consumption behavior? This study sets up a quasi-experiment using the “Project Carbon Zero” campaign, an energy-saving contest in Singapore, to empirically test the effectiveness of school children nudges in bringing electricity conservation messages home and influencing behaviors of their families and neighbors. Based on the 2 kilometers (km) home-school distance as an identification, our results show that families living within 2 km from participating schools (treatment group) used 1.8% less electricity at the block level than other families outside the 2 km school zone (control group) during the contest period. The electricity savings effects are persistent with an estimated marginal savings 1.6% in the post-campaign months. The results imply that policy makers and advocates for energy conservation could use school children nudges in public campaigns, instead of pecuniary interventions, to drive home behavioral changes in electricity conservation of families.
abstract_zh: 孩子能否有效地“推动”父母改变其能源消费行为？本研究利用新加坡的节能竞赛“零碳计划”（Project Carbon Zero）构建准实验，检验学童推动在将节电信息带回家庭、并影响家人与邻居行为方面的有效性。以家与学校之间2公里的距离作为识别依据，我们的结果显示，在竞赛期间，居住在参与学校2公里范围内的家庭（处理组）相比2公里学区之外的其他家庭（对照组），在街区层面的用电量减少了1.8%。竞赛结束后的几个月里，持续的节电效应估计为1.6%的边际节约。研究结果表明，节能倡导者和政策制定者可以在公共宣传活动中利用学童推动，而非货币性干预措施，以促使家庭在节电行为上发生切实改变。
